articles.title: Why has Shafali Verma been reprimanded by the ICC after India's win over Zimbabwe?
articles.summary: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the
articles.body: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe.The incident took place during India's nine-wicket win in Raipur on Sunday. The 22-year-old was found guilty of breaching Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct.What happened during the match?The incident took place in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings. Shafali dropped a catch offered by Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling. She then threw the ball to the ground in frustration.The ICC found that Shafali had breached Article 2.2 of its Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel. This rule deals with the “abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match,” an ICC media release said.One demerit point added to her recordAlong with the official reprimand, one demerit point has been added to Shafali's disciplinary record. This was her first offence in a 24-month period.Shafali admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by G.S. Lakshmi of the ICC International Panel of Match Referees. As a result, there was no need for a formal hearing.On-field umpires Vrinda Rathi and Gayathri Venugopalan, third umpire Anna Harris and fourth umpire Janani Narayanan levelled the charge.What is the penalty for a Level 1 breach?Level 1 breaches of the ICC Code of Conduct carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand. articles.title: ICC T20I Rankings: Shree Charani, Deepti Sharma dominate as Nandani Sharma, Kranti Gaud make gains
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s dominance in the ICC Women’s T20I Bowling Rankings continues, with Shree Charani and Deepti Sharma retaining the top two positions,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s dominance in the ICC Women’s T20I Bowling Rankings continues, with Shree Charani and Deepti Sharma retaining the top two positions, while fast bowlers Nandani Sharma and Kranti Gaud made significant gains following the ongoing series against Zimbabwe.India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series at home, with their bowlers playing a key role in the campaign. The latest rankings reflect the depth of India’s bowling resources, with Nandani and Kranti rewarded for their performances in the first two matches in Raipur.Nandani emerged as one of the biggest movers, climbing 26 places to 45th in the T20I bowling rankings. The right-arm seamer has claimed three wickets across the first two matches, making her one of the joint-leading wicket-takers in the series.Teammate Kranti also made progress, moving up nine places to 43rd. Their rise adds to the achievements of Charani and Deepti, who remain first and second, respectively, after delivering economical performances against Zimbabwe.Shree Charani, Deepti Sharma maintain their gripCharani continues to lead the T20I bowling rankings, with experienced all-rounder Deepti occupying second place. Their continued presence at the summit underlines India’s strength in the shortest format, where spin has remained a key component of the bowling attack.The latest update also highlights the growing contribution of India’s pace options. Nandani’s 26-place jump and Kranti’s rise of nine positions show how the performances of the supporting bowlers are strengthening the team’s resources ahead of future international assignments.New Zealand bowlers and batters make gainsThere were also changes in the T20I rankings following the opening match of the trans-Tasman series between Australia and New Zealand in Sydney.Australia seamer Annabel Sutherland climbed one place to eighth among T20I bowlers, while New Zealand’s Jess Kerr rose five spots to 17th. Teammates Bree Illing and Nensi Patel also improved, moving up six places to 23rd and five places to 35th, respectively.New Zealand batters Maddy Green and Georgia Plimmer made progress in the T20I batting rankings. Green climbed three places to 34th, while Plimmer made a significant 13-place jump to 48th.Australia’s Beth Mooney, meanwhile, retained her position as the world’s top-ranked T20I batter.Megan Schutt, Ellyse Perry rise in ODI rankingsThe latest update also brought gains for Australian players in the ODI rankings following their 50-over series against Bangladesh in the ICC Women’s Championship.Veteran fast bowler Megan Schutt moved up one place to fourth in the ODI bowling rankings. Ellyse Perry climbed one spot to ninth among ODI batters and made an even bigger jump in the all-rounders’ list, rising 14 places to 25th.Sutherland also benefited from her unbeaten half-century in the final ODI, moving up four places to 13th in the batting rankings. articles.title: The Hundred 2027 will allow teams to field four overseas players in playing XI in increase from previous seasons
articles.summary: Faf du Plessis, Shadab Khan and Daryl Mitchell among those to miss out in 2026 auction, who could stand a greater chance of being signed next year as the number of overseas players allowed in a squad increases from four to five, and in playing XIs from three to four
articles.body:
Before the direct signing window from January 20 - February 3, and the auction - set for March but the date yet to confirmed - teams can first look to secure their favourite players from 2026.

Also, in a change to squad sizes for 2027, teams can now carry a maximum of 19 players (and minimum of 16), with the number of overseas players allowed rising from four to five - and from three to four in playing XIs.

Here's everything you need to know about The Hundred retention window and more:

When does the retention window open and close?

The window opened on October 19, 2026 and closes on January 15, 2027. Teams can announce retained players from their 2026 squads at any point during this period.

Each men's and women's squad can retain up to 16 players. Retained players will stay on their 2026 salaries for the 2027 season.

Teams can retain any player signed at The Hundred Auction 2026, including those who subsequently didn't play in the 2026 competition due to injury or unavailability.

They can also retain any replacement player who played at least two games in the 2026 competition.

Players selected in the Vitality Wildcard Draft in 2026 can be retained at their base price or on an increased salary for 2027, but they will not count as wildcards next season if retained.

What happens to players who aren't retained?

Unretained players remain eligible to be signed during the direct signing window, either by their existing team or by another team. They may also choose to enter the auction in March.

The direct signing window runs from January 20 to February 3. During this period, teams can sign eligible players directly before finalising their squads at auction.

As in 2026, teams can make up to four direct signings if they have space in their squad. This includes a maximum of two domestic players and a maximum of two overseas players.

Overseas player and squad size updates for 2027

The maximum number of overseas players in a squad has increased from four to five, with four allowed in the playing XI - up from three. This additional overseas player is only available, should teams opt for it.

Squad sizes have increased to a maximum of 19 players for 2027.

The Hundred Auction will take place in early March 2027. The exact date will be announced in due course.

articles.title: 'Where are the fans?': David Warner fumes over sparse crowds in South Africa-Australia Test series
articles.summary: The ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia has sparked a debate over the popularity of red-ball cricket, with former Australian opener
articles.body: The ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia has sparked a debate over the popularity of red-ball cricket, with former Australian opener David Warner expressing disappointment over the lack of spectators at the venues. Despite featuring the world's top two Test teams, the series has struggled to draw sizeable crowds, prompting Warner to question whether the format is thriving.The stands were largely empty during the opening Test at Kingsmead in Durban, while rain further affected attendance during the first two days of the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha. The sparse crowds have raised concerns, particularly given the stature of the contest and its significance for both sides.David Warner questions Test cricket's popularity"We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving?" Warner wrote on X."You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic," he added.South Africa-Australia series struggles to draw crowdsThe series carries considerable significance, with Australia entering as the world's top-ranked Test side and South Africa placed second. It is also Australia's first Test tour of South Africa since the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, while the Proteas are playing their first home Test series as reigning world Test champions.Despite the high-profile nature of the contest, the turnout has been underwhelming. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Ajay Kookna's twin strikes keep Rajasthan in control against Railways
articles.summary: JAIPUR: Left-arm spinner Ajay Kookna’s timely twin strikes broke two crucial partnerships to derail a solid Railways recovery, keeping Rajasthan firmly in
articles.body: JAIPUR: Left-arm spinner Ajay Kookna’s timely twin strikes broke two crucial partnerships to derail a solid Railways recovery, keeping Rajasthan firmly in the driver’s seat on Day Three at the Sawai Man Singh Stadium. Railways finished the day at 305/6, still trailing by 192 runs behind the hosts' massive first-innings total, despite a gritty 73-run (203 balls) resistance from captain Bhargav Merai.After starting the day from 46/1, Railways lost two quick wickets in the opening session to pacers Danish Bhambhu and Akash Singh before mounting a recovery. Merai first partnered with Eshaan Goyal (64 off 164) to put together 98 runs.Kookna provided the much-needed first breakthrough after lunch by trapping Goyal lbw, ending their threatening stand. Following this, Merai found another fluent ally in Ravi Singh (53 off 75).Explaining the tactical shift after the break, Kookna pointed out that while they initially expected the pitch to offer help, it did not, so the target was simply to restrict runs by hitting consistent areas. “As the ball gets older, it stops turning, so the new ball helped us break the partnership," he said after the day’s play.The Railways’ pair frustrated the hosts with an 83-run alliance, before Kookna halted their momentum in the final session with his second decisive strike of the day, having the Railways skipper stumped.Soon after, pacer Chetan Sharma removed Ravi, who was caught behind, to reduce the visitors to 256/6.The Railways skipper conceded that when that partnership broke, the momentum shifted. “Our partnership was very crucial. If I had stayed at the crease, we would surely have had the upper hand,” he said.Refusing to surrender, Zubair Ali (18 not out off 33 balls) and Toufik Mondal (33 not out off 48 balls) stitched together an unbroken lower-order resistance through the rest of the evening. The pair narrowed the deficit, keeping alive hopes of avoiding the follow-on as the match heads into the final day.Merai said that they were originally looking to chase the 497-run total. “I have seen big totals being chased down here, so that was our goal. If we had scored 300 for 4, we could still be in the game, but we lost two extra wickets. Zubair scored 100 last year and won two Player-of-the-Match awards, so we are still hopeful of a good partnership of 100 runs, and then things can change," he said."The pitch has gone slower. There is some patch at the far end, so Kookna will be crucial for them on the last day. articles.title: Pakistan vs England: Sloppy visitors floored by Arafat Minhas in Rawalpindi
articles.summary: England begin their wandering winter with a sloppy loss to Pakistan in the one-day tri-series in Rawalpindi.
articles.body:
One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi

Pakistan 302-9 (50 overs): Baker 3-65; Nawaz 79 (74), Arafat 59 (58)

England 215 (38.4 overs): Banton 57 (53), Arafat 6-40

England began their wandering winter with a sloppy loss to Pakistan in the one-day tri-series in Rawalpindi.

In the opening match of five separate tours to four different countries on three continents, England's mistakes opened the door for Pakistan's Arafat Minhas to take advantage.

The all-rounder made a crucial 59 with the bat, then bamboozled England by taking 6-40 with his left-arm spin.

Asked to bat, Pakistan were 190-5 in the 37th over when diving wicketkeeper Jordan Cox put down Arafat on 12, one of three catches England dropped.

Arafat, alongside a powerful 79 from Hasan Nawaz, lifted Pakistan to 302-9.

Faced with making the second-highest score to win an ODI at the Rawalpindi Stadium, England made a rapid start to the chase, only for further errors to let Pakistan back in.

At 91-0, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull to depart for 45 and, crucially, Tom Banton was caught for 57 when he shovelled Arafat's long hop to mid-wicket.

Arafat's fine all-round performance continued with a beautiful delivery to bowl England captain Harry Brook for five and Naseem Shah got one to keep low to bowl Joe Root for 33.

When Cox was lbw and Jamie Overton holed out, both off Arafat, England were floored. They spluttered to 215 all out, losing their last seven wickets for 50 runs, capped by a calamitous run out of Gus Atkinson.

Pakistan have two wins from two in the tri-series and are already on the brink of the final, while England next meet Sri Lanka at the same ground on Thursday, with both sides looking for their first victory.

Winter and World Cup countdown start with defeat

Not only is this the beginning of England's winter – two trips to Australia and Test tours of South Africa and Bangladesh follow – but also the start of a long run-in to the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa next year.

This was the first of a potential 21 ODIs in preparation for the World Cup, the tri-series format designed to replicate the pressure and permutations of tournament cricket.

In fairness to England, they have improved in ODI cricket - winning their three previous series this year - and they were without three first-choice players in Jos Buttler, Jofra Archer and Jacob Bethell.

Nevertheless, this was a game they could have won had they not wasted their opportunities, while squad players missed chances to press their case. Cox dropped two catches behind the stumps, Sonny Baker was expensive with the new ball and Banton squandered the platform to make a huge score at the top of the order.

The outcome was a defeat in their first ODI in Pakistan since 2005 and a loss in their first taste of tri-series ODI cricket since 2015.

To focus on England's shortcomings would be a disservice to Pakistan, who are a vastly different proposition in this format on home soil to the team soundly beaten in the Test series in the UK last month.

From 133-5 in the 28th over, the hosts could have wilted, yet Nawaz's slog-sweep for six from the first ball he faced from Adil Rashid was the beginning of Pakistan's fightback.

Along with Arafat and Faheem Ashraf, Nawaz carried Pakistan to what seemed no more than a competitive total on a flat pitch.

When night fell, Arafat produced his magical spell to the delight of a noisy full house.

He produced the best figures by a Pakistan spinner in an ODI against England, then Arafat also ran out Atkinson to complete the hosts' win.

Bavuma epic drags SA back into Test - have they time to beat Australia?

England coach should be English, suggests Fleming

How one rule change is altering the face of one-day cricket

This was a good test for England's batting, not unlike the kind of chase they can expect to face at the World Cup, albeit in different conditions.

Much like when they were tasked with overhauling 325 to beat Sri Lanka at Headingley in an ODI less than a month ago, they fell short.

Banton made a century in that series but knows the injured Bethell will be back for the tour of Australia next month. Another hundred would have made the selection decision difficult, explaining Banton's obvious disappointment when he somehow belted Arafat to Shaheen Afridi.

Cox will have a run in the ODI side because Buttler is out until at least the new year and the Essex man will also have an eye on securing a place in the Test team in South Africa.

At number six, Cox had the opportunity to make amends for his two drops, yet he was deceived by the wily Arafat to be lbw for 18.

In between, England lost their biggest wickets. Brook was all at sea in missing a beautiful turning delivery from Arafat, Root was arguably unlucky to be bowled by Naseem and Sam Curran, playing for the first time since The Hundred, shovelled to deep square leg.

When Curran departed for 27, England were 177-5 midway through the 32nd over and the game was beginning to slip away.

What followed was Arafat singled-handedly ripping through the lower order.

Cox was done in the flight to be leg before, Overton was caught at long-on and Will Jacks, so often England's saviour in white-ball cricket, found the hands of mid-wicket.

Rashid was palpably leg before and the mix-up between Baker and Atkinson that resulted in the latter face down on the turf epitomised England's collapse.

It was another chapter in England's long history of capitulating to spin on the sub-continent.

England captain Harry Brook: "We were quite happy with 300. We thought they were slightly under par. It got dewy as we thought it would do. We were pretty happy at halfway."

On not pushing on after a strong opening partnership: "That was the story of the innings. We thought [Tom] Banton, Ducky [Ben Duckett] set the tone to get a 100 partnership and then it was a case of losing too many wickets in clumps, we couldn't string the partnerships together and we ended up on the wrong side."

On where they will look to do better next time: "You always want to win, don't you? We've spoken a lot about rotation of strike through the middle but I think we were a little too careful against the spinners especially, so we can probably put them under a little bit more pressure in stages and we've got to tonight to talk about it and tomorrow and bounce back better on Thursday."

articles.title: Temba Bavuma hits Test-best 179 as South Africa dominate Australia on day three of second Test in Gqeberha
articles.summary: Kagiso Rabada takes wicket with fourth ball on Test return as South Africa reduce Australia to 3-1 by stumps in Gqeberha, trailing by 422 after Temba Bavuma's earlier 179; watch day four of second Test, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8.30am, Wednesday (play starts 9am)
articles.body:
Bavuma's magnificent innings helped rescue the Proteas from a perilous position of 40-4, with Australia's bowlers on top during the first two rain-affected days in Gqeberha but Bavuma, along with vital lower-order contributions from Marco Jansen (85) and Simon Harmer (82) helped wrestle the match the home side's way.

Kagiso Rabada only added to their advantage by striking with his fourth ball back from a hamstring injury that has sidelined him since June, with Nic Maddinson poking an edge to third slip for his second duck in three innings since his own Test return.

Australia ultimately closed on 3-1, still trailing South Africa by 422 runs on first innings, though with so much time lost to wet weather already in the Test match, the hosts are up against the clock over the final two days in their push for victory and force a series-decider in Cape Town from October 27.

South Africa resumed the third morning on 97-5 and swiftly lost a sixth wicket as Wiaan Mulder (13) was bounced out by Mitchell Starc for his 450th Test wicket.

But Bavuma continued to battle, notching a 140-ball fifty, before he and Jansen provided the perfect counter-punch in a 132-run partnership for the seventh wicket, one which was only bettered by the 183 put with Harmer - a new South African record stand for the eighth wicket.

Scott Boland (5-81), who had torn through the Proteas' top order over the first two days, secured a well-deserved five-for with the dismissal of Jansen, while Harmer and Bavuma's resistance was finally broken with back-to-back deliveries to trigger a declaration on 425-9.

Marnus Labuschagne first bowled Harmer, before Starc was the one to finally draw an error from Bavuma as he nicked off for 179.

Rabada added to Australia's woes with his early dismissal of Maddison, though he was restricted to just the one over as the deteriorating light resulted in three subsequent overs of spin prior to stumps.

Former Australia batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series in South Africa.

South Africa lost the first Test match by 214 runs in Durban , with large sections of the Kingsmead ground empty, and the crowds haven't really picked up through the first two rain-affected days of the second Test in Gqeberha.

"We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa?" Warner said in a social media post on Tuesday.

"Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we're supposed to believe the format is thriving?

"You can't keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it.

"Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic."

Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, was part of the infamous 'sandpapergate' scandal that dominated Australia's last tour of South Africa in 2018. The then vice-captain was given a one-year ban and told he would never be considered for a leadership position within the team again.

articles.title: England slump to defeat against Pakistan in ODI tri-series after faltering chasing 303 in Rawalpindi
articles.summary: England lose last seven wickets for just 50 runs, bowled out for 215 in 38.4 overs chasing 303 to win; wheels come off after opening stand of 91 between Ben Duckett (45) and Tom Banton (57) snapped; Pakistan's Arafat Minhas takes 6-40 and secures winning run out after maiden ODI fifty
articles.body:
England, who have won their last three bilateral ODI series, were cruising on 91-0 inside 15 overs in a chase of 303, only to end up being bowled out for 215 in 38.4, losing their final seven wickets for just 50 runs, as home spinner Arafat Minhas backed up his maiden ODI half-century with figures of 6-40 in a stunning performance.

Visiting captain Harry Brook (5) was bowled by a beauty from Arafat after Ben Duckett (45) and Tom Banton (57) failed to build on a rollicking opening stand against a Pakistan side who had rallied from 81-4 to 302-9 earlier in the day having being put in to bat.

The tourists wilted once the hosts snapped a partnership of 31 from 57 balls between Joe Root (33) and Sam Curran (27) from 128-3, with Arafat on a hat-trick after removing Will Jacks (19) and Adil Rashid (1) from successive deliveries in the 39th over before he ran out Gus Atkinson (7) two balls later to clinch victory.

Arafat was involved in each of the final five wickets, including those of Jamie Overton (1), who holed out at long-on in what commentator Stuart Broad described as "an appalling dismissal", and Jordan Cox (18), who fell lbw.

England are back in action against Sri Lanka at the same venue on Thursday ( 9am UK, live on Sky Sports ) in a tournament which sees the three sides play each other twice before the top two in the table meet in a final in Lahore on October 31.

England strike from first ball of the match

Brook's men - whose feast of white-ball cricket continues in Australia in November with three ODIs and five T20s - were on top at various points on Tuesday, starting from the very first ball when Atkinson (2-35) had Fakhar Zaman (0) caught at midwicket.

Fakhar, pouched low by Root, was one of four batters to fall inside 19 overs, with opening partner Saim Ayub (8) bounced out by seamer Sonny Baker (3-65) after being starved of the strike and Babar Azam (34) bowled playing back to off-spinner Jacks.

When leg-spinner Rashid, back from a hand injury that saw him miss the 2-1 win at home to Sri Lanka in September, had Salman Ali Agha - a centurion against Sri Lanka on Sunday - caught sweeping a full toss, you wondered if Pakistan would bat out the overs.

But Shaheen Shah Afridi's side managed that thanks to a middle and lower-order counterattack led by Hasan Nawaz (79 off 74), who pumped his first ball, bowled by Rashid, for six amid nine boundaries all told during his second ODI fifty.

The 24-year-old shared fifty stands with Arafat (59) and Saad Baig (35), while there was then an alliance of 72 from just 49 deliveries between Arafat and Faheem Ashraf (39 off 26).

England sloppy in the field before fluffing lines with the bat

England, who conceded 80 runs from the final eight overs, dropped three catches - Atkinson with one of them and Cox, deputising as wicketkeeper for the injured Jos Buttler (hamstring), guilty of two - while Curran (1-40 off five overs) looked rusty with the ball having not played since The Hundred in August owing to a groin problem.

Pakistan's total was looking ever so lean as Banton and Duckett fired early on - Banton notching his third successive fifty-plus score and third in four knocks since replacing Jacob Bethell (knee) at the top of the order.

However, when Duckett was bounced out by Haris Rauf (2-32) and Arafat had Banton cloth to midwicket and castled Brook with a peach that straightened after gripping, the wobble was on.

Root and Curran stemmed Pakistan's fightback initially, only for Root to be poleaxed by a Naseem Shah ball that kept low and Curran to heave Rauf to deep backward square.

articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Temba Bavuma century drags hosts back into series
articles.summary: Captain Temba Bavuma drags South Africa back into their Test series against Australia but did his side bat on too long on day three?
articles.body:
Second Test, Gqeberha (day three of five)

South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81

Captain Temba Bavuma dragged South Africa back into their Test series against Australia with a masterful 179 on day three in Gqeberha.

Bavuma, who emerged in the gloom at 12-2 on day one, batted for 552 minutes across three days in making his highest Test score, allowing the Proteas to declare on 425-9 with half an hour to play having been 110-6 earlier on day three.

Kagiso Rabada nicked off Australia opener Nic Maddinson in the first over of Australia's reply to further boost the hosts' cause.

Bavuma's knock was every bit as impressive as Matthew Renshaw's 190 for Australia in their first Test win - arguably more so given the momentum that had built behind Australia since South Africa's batting struggles and the quality of the tourists' attack.

He remained composed in sharing partnerships of 132 with Marco Jansen and 183 with number nine Simon Harmer - the best eighth-wicket partnership in South Africa's Test history.

The century was Bavuma's fifth in Tests - 10 years after his first made him the first Black African to score a Test hundred for the Proteas.

He said it was "definitely" one of his best innings.

"That bowling attack, at least three are in the top 10 of the bowling rankings," he added. "There is a reason why."

More relevant for this series and England's tour to come over Christmas, it was Bavuma's fourth century in 14 Tests as South Africa captain.

He now averages 54.36 as Test skipper, compared with 34.53 across 93 innings before taking the reins. Few can match that improvement.

Should South Africa have declared earlier?

It was Bavuma's dismissal - caught behind off Mitchell Starc - which triggered South Africa's decision to declare with half an hour to go in the day.

They had resisted doing so earlier in the session and when Harmer was bowled by Marnus Labuschagne a ball before the Bavuma wicket.

With the floodlights on and skies dark, conditions were perfect for seam bowling when Australia's reply began. Maddinson was only able to resist four deliveries before nicking to third slip.

The umpires then deemed the light too poor for seam bowling to continue, however, and after three overs of spin with the new ball the players left the field.

Had South Africa declared earlier, Jansen could have bowled in tandem with Rabada in the gloom.

"There was thought of that," Bavuma said. "I was a little hesitant because of the weather.

"If we [had declared] a bit early we would have got one or two more overs. Saying that we got the one we wanted.

"Right now I hope things go our way and we set ourselves to be on the field for the majority of those two days."

After only 42 overs were possible across the first two days, South Africa now have an outside shot at victory over days four and five, ideally by dismissing Australia cheaply and enforcing the follow-on.

"We have given ourselves a chance," Bavuma said.

"There is the other side of the draw but going into [the third Test in] Cape Town whatever the confidence we can get here, being able to put their bowlers on their feet for a considerable amount of time, hopefully that can pay off in the long run."

articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur unleashes six-hitting blitz as India thrash Zimbabwe by 92 runs to complete 3-0 T20I series sweep
articles.summary: India’s women turned Raipur into a six-hitting spectacle, with Shafali Verma and Harmanpreet Kaur unleashing a batting assault before Nandani Sharma’s
articles.body: India’s women turned Raipur into a six-hitting spectacle, with Shafali Verma and Harmanpreet Kaur unleashing a batting assault before Nandani Sharma’s three-wicket haul sealed a 92-run victory over Zimbabwe in the third T20I on Tuesday. The emphatic win completed a 3-0 series sweep for the Women in Blue, extended their winning streak in the format to 11 matches and handed them their biggest T20I victory by run margin on home soil.Shafali smashed 69 off 37 balls, while Harmanpreet rolled back the years with an unbeaten 91 off just 41 deliveries as India piled up 216/7 after opting to bat. Zimbabwe showed greater resistance than in their previous outings, with Sharne Mayers scoring a fighting 60, but Nandani’s 3/18 ensured the visitors finished at 124/7 in their 20 overs.India’s victory also marked Zimbabwe’s 23rd consecutive defeat in women’s T20Is, underlining the gulf between the sides despite a spirited individual effort from Mayers.Shafali, Anushka provide explosive startWith India already leading the series 2-0, Smriti Mandhana opted to bat first and used the opportunity to give the middle order more time in the middle. Anushka Sharma was promoted to open alongside Shafali, while Mandhana held herself back.The move paid dividends as the opening pair added 54 runs off just 32 balls. Anushka struck 28 off 20 deliveries, including a powerful six off Tendai Makusha in the fifth over, while Shafali continued her aggressive approach at the other end.The opener brought up her second consecutive half-century, peppering the leg-side boundary with a series of sixes over deep midwicket. She also used the sweep effectively against the spinners, ensuring Zimbabwe struggled to build pressure during the powerplay and middle overs.Shafali eventually departed for 69 off 37 balls, having provided India with the platform for another imposing total.Harmanpreet returns to destructive bestHarmanpreet took charge after Shafali’s dismissal, producing a commanding innings that showcased her power-hitting at its best. The India captain struck an unbeaten 91 off 41 balls, including five sixes, as the hosts maintained their scoring momentum.The 37-year-old had struggled to find her rhythm on the slower surfaces during the Women’s Asia Cup and had limited opportunities to bat during India’s triumphant Asian Games campaign in Japan. Tuesday’s innings offered a timely reminder of her ability to dominate an attack when conditions favour stroke-making.India accelerated spectacularly at the death, plundering 62 runs in the final five overs despite losing four wickets. Their total of 216/7 left Zimbabwe facing a steep challenge.Mayers fights back, but Zimbabwe fall shortZimbabwe’s chase suffered an immediate setback when Kelis Ndhlovu was dismissed for a first-ball duck. Mayers, however, refused to let the innings drift, counterattacking with a muscular knock that kept the visitors in the contest for a period.She scored 60 off 49 balls, striking four boundaries and four sixes, and found support from Beloved Biza as Zimbabwe attempted to rebuild after the early loss. Mayers’ innings was the standout contribution in a chase that otherwise lacked sustained partnerships.India rotated their bowling resources, using seven bowlers during the innings. Nandani emerged as the pick of the attack, taking three wickets for 18 runs to break Zimbabwe’s resistance and prevent any late surge.Zimbabwe eventually closed on 124/7, finishing 92 runs short of the target.The victory gave India a 3-0 clean sweep in the three-match series and extended their winning run in women’s T20Is to 11 matches, including their campaigns in the Asia Cup in the UAE and the Asian Games in Japan.The result was also India's biggest home victory by run margin in the format. articles.title: England captain Harry Brook laments 'wickets in clumps' in ODI batting collapse as Arafat Minhas stars for Pakistan
articles.summary: Arafat Minhas scored 59 off 58 balls to help Pakistan to 302-9 before taking a career-best 6-40, seeing England bowled out for 215 in Rawalpindi; England next face Sri Lanka on Thursday, live from 8.30am on Sky Sports Cricket (first ball 9am)
articles.body:
Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball in Rawalpindi for the hosts, who recovered from 133-5 to post 302-9 from their 50 overs before skittling England for 215 to claim their second win of the tournament.

Pakistan's all-rounder fired 59 off 58 deliveries and was part of a strong lower middle-order fightback, with Hasan Nawaz top-scoring with a 74-ball 79 and Faheem Ashraf adding 39 off 26 deliveries in the closing overs.

Tom Banton and Ben Duckett shifted the momentum in England's favour with a 91-run opening stand, only for Arafat to bamboozle the visitors with a career-best 6-40 and help Pakistan wrap up victory with more than 11 overs to spare.

"We thought they [Pakistan] were slightly under par," Brook said after their defeat. "It got dewy, as we thought it would do and we were pretty happy at halfway.

" We thought [Tom] Banton, Ducky [Ben Duckett] set the tone to nearly get a 100 partnership and then it was a case of losing too many wickets in clumps. We couldn't really string the partnerships together and we ended up on the wrong side.

" We've spoken a lot about rotation of strike through the middle but I think we were a little too careful against the spinners especially, so we can probably put them under a little bit more pressure in stages.

"We've got to tonight to talk about it and tomorrow and bounce back better on Thursday."

England were well placed at 165-3 - despite Arafat removing Banton (57) and Brook (five) - when Naseem Shah bowled Joe Root for 33, with the tourists still in a good position until losing their last five wickets for 18 runs in a chaotic five-over spell.

Jordan Cox was trapped lbw by Arafat before Pakistan's spinner removed Jamie Overton in his next over, with the manner of the dismissal criticised by former England bowler Stuart Broad on commentary.

"That's appalling batting," Broad told Sky Sports, having seen England slip to 205-7. "With Will Jacks at the other end, you're saying England have a chance, you play for your partner.

"You say you have a weakness against spin, that's certainly not what you do - he's just chipped it down long-on's throat. A poor wicket for England to lose."

Arafat closed out victory by being involved in all three final wickets, coming in the space of four balls, dismissing Jacks and Adil Rashid in successive deliveries before running out Gus Atkinson.

He became the third Pakistan all-rounder - after Abdul Razzaq and Shahid Afridi - to grab a five-wicket haul and score a half-century in an ODI, with the 21-year-old proud of his man-of-the-match display.

"Hasan [Nawaz] and I discussed that we need to bat deep," Arafat said. "I took charge after Hasan got out and I tried to bat until the end of the innings, which helped in taking the score beyond 300."

On his bowling, Arafat added: "I kept my plans simple. I think variations are very important for a spinner, as they help in deceiving the opposition batters."

Pakistan take plaudits as England need to 'learn from mistakes'

Victory for Pakistan is their second successive win in the ODI tri-series, following their 37-run win over Sri Lanka in the tournament opener, keeping them top of the standings and leaving them well-placed to qualify for the final on October 31.

"A bit of credit to Pakistan, who in both innings fought back," former England captain Nasser Hussain told Sky Sports . "They were 81-4 and 133-5 and yet managed to get over 300.

"England were going well and everyone was thinking they were going to win this game, but there was a bit of fight and a bit of character from Pakistan - with bat and ball."

England - missing several key players - have won all three ODI series this year after losing six of seven bilateral series before that, with Hussain expecting them to take lessons from their convincing defeat.

"He [Sam Curran] looks a bit short of a gallop at the moment, both with the ball and with the bat," Hussain added. "He didn't have rhythm, but that will come. Adil Rashid will get better the more he bowls - he's obviously coming back from injury.

"They are missing Jos Butler - England's greatest ever white-ball player. They're missing Jofra Archer and they're also missing Jacob Bethell.

"They've been on a good track, so don't get too up when you win and don't get too down when you haven't chased 300 - just learn from the mistakes that you made today."

articles.title: ‘Play the ball as late as possible’: Sunil Gavaskar’s advice to India batters for New Zealand Tests
articles.summary: Mumbai: Sunil Gavaskar has advised India’s batters to play the ball as late as possible when they face New Zealand in the two-Test series in Wellington
articles.body: Mumbai: Sunil Gavaskar has advised India’s batters to play the ball as late as possible when they face New Zealand in the two-Test series in Wellington and Christchurch, where swing and seam are expected to pose a major challenge.India struggled on their last Test tour of New Zealand in February-March 2020, losing 0-2 after managing totals of 165, 191, 242 and 124. With green pitches likely again, Gavaskar said patience and technique would be vital.“Like in England, you try and play as late as possible. Don’t commit yourself too much, because that gives you the chance to cover the movement off the pitch,” Gavaskar said.“When there is movement in the air, you can see it and react. But after pitching, the movement happens very close to the bat. The later you play, the better your chances of scoring runs and defending the good ball. Don’t push at the ball. Defend with soft hands, not hard hands.”The batting great also questioned the decision to schedule only two Tests, saying every series in the next World Test Championship cycle should have at least three matches.“Ideally, there should be a minimum of three Tests. Two Tests don’t always give you a result. One team could win one match and the other team the next. A third Test gives you a better opportunity to win a series,” he said.He believes India will benefit from having spent an extended period in New Zealand before the Tests, with the team already playing five T20Is and five ODIs on the tour.“One of the biggest problems in New Zealand is getting your body clock used to the time difference. It takes a really long time for your sleep and waking hours to adjust. The Indian team being there already is going to be a big plus,” Gavaskar said.He warned that early-summer conditions could make batting difficult but said runs would be available once batters settled in.“There will be a fair bit of grass, cooler weather and the possibility of rain. The ball will move in the air and after pitching, so it won’t be easy. But once you settle down, these can be some of the best pitches to bat on. I’m hoping our batters get going,” he said.Gavaskar also backed India’s pace attack to challenge New Zealand.“With Jasprit Bumrah leading the attack and Mohammed Siraj around, we have the capability of surprising the New Zealand batting unit. We’ve got a good team. As with everything, you need a little bit of luck,” he said.(Tune-in: Watch India’s tour of New Zealand live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV, starting October 22, 2026.)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Who will talk to me, and why?’: Mohammed Shami’s blunt take after India selectors overlook him
articles.summary: Mohammed Shami remains determined to fight his way back into the Indian team, insisting that he is still at the peak of his fitness despite being
articles.body: Mohammed Shami remains determined to fight his way back into the Indian team, insisting that he is still at the peak of his fitness despite being overlooked for the upcoming all-format tour of New Zealand.The 36-year-old fast bowler, who last represented India in March 2025, has been left out of the squad for the New Zealand tour even as questions continue over the team's bowling resources, particularly in the shorter formats. Meanwhile, his contemporary Bhuvneshwar Kumar has returned to the national side after a gap of nearly four years.Speaking to reporters after Bengal's Ranji Trophy victory over Services, Shami made it clear that the prospect of playing for India again continues to motivate him. He also stressed that he remains committed to domestic cricket and has no intention of abandoning his ambitions."Hope should always be there (for India comeback). In any profession, in any sport, you should have a goal. Everyone has a goal. Today we are playing for Ranji Trophy and playing for the title. There is always a goal and there should be a goal," Shami said.When a reporter referred to the period when he was at the peak of his fitness, the pacer was quick to challenge the suggestion that those days were behind him."Sir, aaj bhi hum peak par hi hain (I am still at my peak). There is no point in lying. Ham jaise bhi hain apne peak par hain (I am very much at my peak)," said Shami, who did not feature against Services because of the conditions.‘Nobody knows when and where I will have to play for India’Shami insisted that missing out on the New Zealand tour had not left him disappointed. Instead, his focus remains on playing regularly, maintaining his rhythm and staying ready for whatever opportunities come his way."It's not a matter of disappointment. I played the whole domestic season last year as well. I played all the matches. My motive is the same. I should play as much as I can. I should be prepared for all the upcoming series and tournaments."Nobody knows when and where I will have to play for India. Even for IPL, playing domestic cricket will be good for me. If I play domestic or white ball, my preparation will be the same. I will play as many matches as I can. My rhythm will be good."The fast bowler also played down the need to look too far ahead towards next year's ODI World Cup in South Africa, saying his immediate priority was to keep improving."I don't think so far. Today we are playing cricket. Tomorrow we don't know what will happen to someone or what the situation will be. There is no point in thinking so far."Whatever matches you are getting, you keep playing and keep improving yourself. I always say that your focus should be on your skill, your fitness," he said.Shami's blunt response on communication with selectorsAsked whether he had spoken to the national selectors over the past year, Shami responded with a pointed question of his own, highlighting his absence from the Indian team.“Sir, I am not in the Indian team, who will talk to me? And why will they talk to me?" he said.While Shami remains outside the national setup, he welcomed Bhuvneshwar's return, suggesting that the veteran seamer's form warranted an earlier recall.Shami also reiterated his strong connection with Bengal, crediting the team for the career he has built and vowing to remain committed to the side."This team has given me this name. This is all because of this team. The day I end my career, it will be with this team. You should be loyal, you should be dedicated. articles.title: Temba Bavuma enters record books with captain’s knock as South Africa produce great fightback
articles.summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma produced a record-breaking innings against Australia, registering his highest Test score and helping his side recover
articles.body: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma produced a record-breaking innings against Australia, registering his highest Test score and helping his side recover from a precarious position to post a formidable total on Day 3 of the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha on Tuesday.Bavuma's 179 is the fourth-highest individual score by a South African captain in a home Test, behind Hashim Amla's 208 against West Indies in Centurion in 2014, Amla's 201 against England in Cape Town in 2016 and Graeme Smith's 183 against England in Cape Town in 2010.The knock also ranks as the second-highest Test score at Gqeberha, behind Herschelle Gibbs' 196 against India in 2001.Bavuma's innings proved crucial after South Africa slumped to 110-6, putting the hosts in danger of surrendering control of the contest. The skipper held the innings together, batting for 334 deliveries and striking 18 fours and a six as South Africa declared at 425-9.The recovery was among the most remarkable in Test cricket. South Africa's total was the second-highest innings score by a team after losing six wickets for 110 runs or fewer, behind England's 446 against Pakistan at Lord's in 2010, when they had been reduced to 102-7.Bavuma had walked in at 12-2 on the opening day and remained at the crease as South Africa slipped to 92-5 amid rain and a wet outfield on the following day. His patience and composure proved decisive as the lower order rallied around him.Marco Jansen provided the first major support, adding 132 runs with Bavuma for the seventh wicket. Jansen scored 85 before being dismissed by Scott Boland, who finished with figures of 5-81.Simon Harmer then joined his captain and the pair put together a decisive 183-run partnership for the eighth wicket. Harmer contributed 82, his maiden Test half-century, to help swing the contest in South Africa's favour.Bavuma reached his fifth Test century off 226 balls before accelerating to surpass his previous best of 172 against West Indies in Johannesburg in 2023. His innings ended when Mitchell Starc dismissed him, with South Africa declaring soon afterwards.Australia faced a difficult finish to the day, losing Nic Maddinson for a four-ball duck to Kagiso Rabada. The visitors were 3-1 at stumps.Australia won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0. South Africa, the reigning World Test champions, are looking to respond as both sides target a place in the 2027 World Test Championship final.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pat Cummins registers unwanted career record as South Africa pull off stunning fightback
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins endured a difficult outing with the ball as South Africa mounted a remarkable recovery in the second Test at St George’s
articles.body: Australia captain Pat Cummins endured a difficult outing with the ball as South Africa mounted a remarkable recovery in the second Test at St George’s Park in Gqeberha, with his figures of 0/96 ranking as the second-most expensive wicketless return of his career.Cummins conceded 96 runs without taking a wicket, better only than his 0/101 against India in Sydney in 2019. The expensive spell came as South Africa recovered from 110-6 to declare at 425-9 on Day 3, putting Australia under pressure after a dramatic turnaround.South Africa’s lower order made the most of the opportunity after the hosts lost their sixth wicket early in the morning session. Captain Temba Bavuma led the fightback with a career-best 179, while Marco Jansen scored 85 and Simon Harmer contributed 82.The recovery was particularly significant in statistical terms. South Africa scored 315 runs after losing their sixth wicket, the second-highest such total in a Test innings. Their effort fell just short of the 318 runs they added against Australia at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in 2008.Australia have also conceded only one higher total after taking the sixth wicket: the 363 runs West Indies scored at Bridgetown in 1955. South Africa's 318-run effort in Melbourne in 2008 is the other entry ahead of the latest Gqeberha performance.The hosts had been in serious trouble at 110-6 after Wiaan Mulder fell for 13 to Mitchell Starc, who claimed his 450th Test wicket. Bavuma and Jansen initially steadied the innings with a 132-run seventh-wicket partnership before Jansen was dismissed by Scott Boland, who finished with 5-81.Harmer then joined Bavuma and the pair added 183 runs for the eighth wicket, turning the innings around. Harmer struck 10 fours and a six in his maiden Test half-century before being bowled by Marnus Labuschagne.Bavuma, meanwhile, reached his fifth Test century off 226 balls and went past his previous best of 172 against West Indies in Johannesburg in 2023. He eventually fell to Starc, bringing the innings to a close soon afterwards.Australia lost Nic Maddinson for a four-ball duck to Kagiso Rabada late in the day and were 3-1 at stumps.Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur breaks down  on live TV after sensational 91, reveals what has changed
articles.summary: Harmanpreet Kaur struggled to hold back her emotions after producing a stunning comeback with the bat, smashing an unbeaten 91 off just 41 balls against
articles.body: Harmanpreet Kaur struggled to hold back her emotions after producing a stunning comeback with the bat, smashing an unbeaten 91 off just 41 balls against Zimbabwe in the third and final T20I. The former India captain's emotional moment came during an innings-break interview, when she reflected on her return to form and thanked those who had backed her through a difficult period.The 37-year-old, who stepped down as India's captain across formats earlier this month, had gone 10 matches without a half-century. Her struggles with the bat had continued through the Women's T20 Asia Cup and the Asian Games, even as India went on to win both tournaments comfortably.But against Zimbabwe, Harmanpreet looked a different batter, finding her rhythm and striking the ball with authority. Her unbeaten knock featured 10 fours and five sixes, with several powerful hits down the ground.As she spoke to the host broadcaster at the break, the 37-year-old became emotional and struggled to hold back her tears."It feels great. Just wanted to enjoy myself, and great that I got some time in the middle and really enjoyed myself on the field," she said.During the conversation, Harmanpreet also acknowledged former India women's team head coach WV Raman, who was part of the broadcast, for his words of encouragement."I just wanted to bat as long as possible, and glad that I was able to do that. I think I should give credit to you also (to WV Raman)."The moment we came, you stepped in and you said, 'Now you do what you want to do,' and that's what I want to do, and really want to enjoy myself. Thanks for those words."Harmanpreet said stepping down as captain had eased the pressure on her, allowing her to focus on enjoying her time in the middle."I don't think there is any pressure anymore. Now it's all about going out there and enjoying myself on the field, and that's exactly what I want to do," she said.She also credited the time spent working in the nets after the Asian Games, thanking batting coach Himanshu Chawla for helping her prepare for the innings."After the Asian Games, I got some time in the nets. I really want to thank Himanshu bhaiya, who's been working really hard on me, and today's batting was all him."The knock marked Harmanpreet's first half-century since beginning her stint as a non-captain. Her unbeaten 91 was also the second-highest individual score by an Indian batter at No. 4 or lower in Women's T20Is, behind her own 103 against New Zealand at Providence during the 2018 T20 World Cup.Speaking at the post-match presentation, Harmanpreet explained how an early boundary helped her assess the conditions and play with greater confidence."I think I hit the (second) ball for four, and that was when I realised it was a good pitch where the ball was coming on nicely to the bat. I gained a lot of confidence from that shot, so I just thought, 'Let me keep going and see how it goes'," she said.She added that continuing to work on her batting and repeating the processes developed in training would be crucial going forward."Batting is key for me, and I just want to keep working on it and repeating those processes in the nets. I really want to give credit to my batting coach (Himanshu Chawla), Manju bhaiya (Munish Bali), who have been working very hard with me and understand the kind of batting I can do."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'He can't walk in right now': Shreyas Iyer says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has 'more years to get opportunities'
articles.summary: India T20 captain Shreyas Iyer has made it clear that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait for regular opportunities in the playing XI, with established
articles.body: India T20 captain Shreyas Iyer has made it clear that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will have to wait for regular opportunities in the playing XI, with established openers Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson continuing to deliver at the top of the order.Despite the teenager's impressive rise, Iyer believes there is no need to rush his integration into the side, pointing out that India's current opening combination has been performing consistently and played a key role in the team's successful defence of the T20 World Cup title earlier this year.Speaking on the eve of India's five-match T20I series against New Zealand, Iyer stressed that the 15-year-old has plenty of time to establish himself at the international level and should remain comfortable within the team environment while waiting for his opportunities."It's important that a talent like him (Sooryavanshi) should always be happy around the dressing room," Iyer said."He is very young, he has more years to get opportunities. It's not like he can walk in right now, because our openers are scoring consistently, and they have won the World Cup."Sooryavanshi was included in India's squads for the England and Ireland tours earlier this year. However, he has featured in only eight of the 21 T20Is India have played since then, with Abhishek and Samson largely retaining their places as the first-choice opening pair.The youngster was given an opportunity to open during the Asian Games, where Samson moved down to No. 3 to accommodate him at the top of the order.While Iyer does not expect Sooryavanshi to walk straight into the playing XI, he believes the experience of touring overseas and getting a feel for different conditions will benefit the youngster in the long run."So, if you see, when he is coming overseas, he will get a fair idea how to play on these particular wickets."Next time, whenever he comes in these conditions, he will be very well-prepared. articles.title: 'We were lacking that': Shreyas Iyer makes big admission as Bhuvneshwar Kumar returns
articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer is looking forward to having Bhuvneshwar Kumar back in the T20I setup, believing the veteran pacer's recent performances in the
articles.body: India captain Shreyas Iyer is looking forward to having Bhuvneshwar Kumar back in the T20I setup, believing the veteran pacer's recent performances in the Indian Premier League (IPL) have demonstrated his ability to excel in the shortest format.Bhuvneshwar could return to international cricket in the five-match T20I series against New Zealand, with the first match scheduled to be played in Christchurch. The comeback would come nearly four years after his last appearance for India in the format, in November 2022.His anticipated return against the West Indies at home was washed out by rain recently, leaving fans waiting a little longer to see the experienced swing bowler back in Indian colours.Since his last T20I appearance, Bhuvneshwar has enjoyed a resurgence with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB), playing a key role in the franchise's back-to-back IPL title triumphs in 2025 and 2026. He has claimed 45 wickets in 31 matches during this period, averaging 22.55 at an economy rate of 8.52.His latest IPL campaign was particularly impressive. Bhuvneshwar finished as the tournament's second-highest wicket-taker, collecting 28 wickets in 16 matches at an average of 17.89 and an economy rate of 7.95.Speaking to reporters ahead of the opening T20I, Iyer highlighted the experience the 36-year-old would bring to an Indian bowling attack that has featured several new faces."He brings a lot of experience to the team. And we were lacking that. Especially after IPL. We had a lot of new bowlers. But in T20, if you see his career graph, he has won IPL in the last two years. So, he has a very good idea of dominating this format," Iyer said.Bhuvneshwar has taken 90 wickets in 87 T20Is for India at an average of 23.10. His record includes two five-wicket hauls and three four-wicket hauls.He is now 10 wickets away from becoming the fifth Indian bowler to claim 100 T20I wickets, joining Arshdeep Singh (145), Jasprit Bumrah (126), Hardik Pandya (114) and Axar Patel (113).The veteran pacer is also approaching another significant career milestone. With 294 international wickets across formats, he needs six more to reach 300, a mark achieved by only 13 Indian bowlers so far. Reaching the landmark would make him the 14th Indian bowler overall and the ninth fast bowler from the country to do so.Iyer anticipates pace challenge in New ZealandBeyond Bhuvneshwar's return, Iyer expects India's batters to face a stern examination from New Zealand's pace-heavy attack. He stressed the importance of adapting quickly to the local conditions and using the practice sessions to develop a clear plan."If we look at the conditions here, fast bowling suits here. I have been here before, and it is not like the conditions are completely different. In England, the way we played, they had prepared the wickets according to our batting. But on a given day, no one knows how the wicket will be. So, we will try to acclimatise as soon as possible. And once we have a good practice session, every individual will get a fair idea of how to plan," he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We have plans for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi': New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner ahead of T20I series vs India
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could be a tough batter to stop if he gets a chance in India's playing XI for the
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could be a tough batter to stop if he gets a chance in India's playing XI for the five-match T20I series. The series begins on Thursday, and Santner said his team has already worked on plans to deal with the young left-hander.Sooryavanshi has not played regularly for India since being picked for the tour of the UK earlier this year. Regular openers Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been doing well, limiting his chances. However, Santner believes the 15-year-old has an important role to play for India, whether in this series or in the future.New Zealand have plans for SooryavanshiSantner said New Zealand have studied Sooryavanshi's aggressive batting, including his performances in the IPL. The Kiwi captain also pointed out that Indian batters faced short-pitched bowling during the England tour."He (Sooryavanshi) did not play in the last series (against West Indies), but we know how good he is, in IPL. We know other players like Abhishek are doing very well. But he (Sooryavanshi) has a huge part to play for India, whether it's in this series or not, but in future," Santner said at the pre-series press conference on Wednesday."If he does get a crack at this series, we've seen what he can do and guys have found it quite hard to stop him. I know in England, they went quite short and hard at a lot of the Indian batters. I think we've seen him in the IPL and how aggressive he can be. So we've got some plans for him if he happens to play."Santner expects Bhuvneshwar to enjoy New Zealand conditionsSantner also spoke about the return of veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar to India's T20I team after an absence of nearly four years.The New Zealand captain expects Bhuvneshwar to be effective in local conditions, especially with the new ball."I think Bhuvi will love these conditions in New Zealand. If there's anything in the wicket, he finds something out of it. On some flat ones in India, he still managed to nip the ball and swing the ball, so I think with the new ball out here, especially, it'll be a challenge (for New Zealand)."In India, it's pretty challenging as a bowler these days. We've seen in the recent series, 250 getting chased down. Who wants to be a bowler, but he (Bhuvneshwar) might like it out here a little bit better."Santner hopes bowlers will have their saySantner is hoping the series will give bowlers a chance to dominate, although he warned that conditions could change quickly."I hope so. I think maybe the first game it might be, but it can change pretty quickly. It's very weather dependent. The second game is a used pitch, same pitch we used for first game. It could be a bit flatter."If it nips around, we've got to play accordingly. If it's flat, you've got to play accordingly," said the 34-year-old left-arm spinner.Santner added that Indian batters have enough experience to handle different conditions around the world."If there is a little bit in it, you might have to change a few shots, but they've played on fast, bouncy wickets before. They've played all around the world and done really well. It's going to be a challenge this series and we're looking forward to it," he added.Santner backs India but expects a challengeSantner acknowledged India's strength ahead of the series, while pointing out that conditions in New Zealand will be different from those at home."They (India) are a well-gelled team and playing some good cricket. We know the conditions will be a little bit different to what they've had at home. The pitches here will be a little bit bouncy. I guess there's still memories and a lot of this group were at the World Cup."And obviously the series beforehand where India beat us 4-1. So again, we know that they're a great team and have done it for a long time."Santner said the conditions could give New Zealand a slight advantage, but both teams will need contributions from their entire squads."We're going around the country, conditions can change. I think both teams are changing a little bit just with the schedule and the quick turnaround. So with the new ball out here especially, he'll be a challenge.”Why Bhuvneshwar could be New Zealand’s biggest early threatBhuvneshwar’s strength lies in his ability to move the ball both ways, trouble batters with his control and make the most of even limited assistance from the surface. articles.title: Hardik Pandya could return only in IPL 2027: Report details India all-rounder's injury timeline, set to miss SL, ZIM series
articles.summary: Hardik Pandya could be sidelined until IPL 2027, with the India all-rounder reportedly set to miss the upcoming Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe series due to injury.
articles.body:
Hardik Pandya could return only in IPL 2027 as he recovers from a shin stress injury.

He is expected to resume jogging in three weeks and miss India 's New Zealand , Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe series.

With domestic cricket unlikely to offer a timely return, the IPL could be his next competitive assignment.

Hardik Pandya's recovery timeline raises concerns over India return

Hardik Pandya may have to wait long until 2027 before he comes back to play in international cricket after being hampered by a repetitive issue of the injury on his shin.

As reported by Abhishek Tripathi of Dainik Jagran, Pandya is currently recuperating at BCCI's Center of Excellence (CoE) due to the injury on his shin caused by stress fracture on the inner part of his shin bone.

Pandya is said to be recovering slowly and the medical team has not yet fixed a date for his comeback in any competitive cricket match. The India all-rounder is likely to resume jogging in around three weeks and subsequently, increase his running gradually over a period of eight weeks, depending on his performance in rehabilitation.

Even after the recovery from the above stage, Pandya needs to regain enough fitness to play at international level.

Which India series will Hardik Pandya miss?

Pandya is set to miss the New Zealand series, with his fitness for further tours of India in question.

There is a limited-overs series against Sri Lanka starting on December 13 and another against Zimbabwe beginning on January 3. According to Tripathi's report, Pandya will most likely miss both the series.

He may miss the rest of the domestic schedule as well, with Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy and Vijay Hazare Trophy concluding before he is ready to make a comeback.

The India-Australia Border-Gavaskar series consisting of five Test matches is set to start on January 21 and end on March 3. However, Pandya is not part of India's Test plans; therefore, the only big series left is the IPL series.

Without any specific date for his comeback, it seems that Pandya might come back directly for IPL 2027.

India must take a long-term view of Hardik Pandya's injury

The prospect of Pandya's unavailability till IPL 2027 could be considered unfortunate for India as Pandya is known for his skills as a fast-bowling all-rounder, providing flexibility in bat and ball. The fitness problems associated with him have led the side to search for other options.

India, however, should refrain from bringing him back before getting fit again, and his rehab should help him build up the workload for him to play consistently with bat and ball.

Considering that the 2027 World Cup is round the corner, India may benefit more from focusing on Pandya's fitness rather than bringing him back prematurely.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan has three major batting milestones in sight as India prepare for the five-match T20I series against New Zealand, starting in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan has three major batting milestones in sight as India prepare for the five-match T20I series against New Zealand, starting in Christchurch on Thursday. articles.summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma has revealed how batting great Sachin Tendulkar has influenced his technique, explaining how he has tried to adapt the
articles.body: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma has revealed how batting great Sachin Tendulkar has influenced his technique, explaining how he has tried to adapt the Indian legend's approach to suit his own game.Bavuma made the admission after scoring a career-best 179 against Australia in the second Test at St George's Park, helping South Africa recover from 110/6 to post 425/9 declared.Asked about the similarities between his technique and that of Tendulkar, one of his heroes, Bavuma said he had consciously tried to incorporate aspects of the former India batter's approach, particularly his movement and ability to play the ball close to his body."Yeah, I mean, I try to emulate my technique to his. I mean, I'm obviously not a big guy. I'm not really going to get any big strides in. I try to be efficient in terms of my movement. Sometimes it gets me into trouble. But I think for me, that's generally what works. I try to play the ball as close to my body as possible," Bavuma said.The South African skipper's 179, which came off 334 balls, was his highest Test score, surpassing his previous best of 172 against the West Indies in 2023. He admitted that the innings was particularly satisfying given his recent struggles to find rhythm."Yeah, definitely one of my better ones. I think looking at the situation of the game, and I think personally as well, I found myself a lot in those type of situations, coming in early, trying to manage myself to kind of scramble through to a 50 or 60, but I think what was nice and the ability just to take it even further and make it count," he said.Bavuma also spoke about the challenge of facing Australia's formidable bowling attack, which includes several highly ranked Test bowlers. Having failed to make a significant contribution in the first Test, he was keen to make amends."So, I mean, we got a taste of it in the first Test, and we kind of knew what was up for us. So I think for me, obviously not being able to contribute from the first Test and then coming in here in the second Test, I think that was a big thing on my mind. But yeah, I was glad I was able to put in a good contribution for the team," he said.The 36-year-old credited his work in the nets for helping him rediscover his touch after a difficult run through the ODI series and the first Test."I think I just haven't had any rhythm, to be honest with you. I kind of struggled with rhythm through the ODI series, even coming up to the first Test. So I think it was just a case of just trying to find a feeling. It can be a bit tricky when you haven't played for months. Yeah, I was just trying to go into the nets and just trying to find the feeling that I kind of had last year," Bavuma said.Bavuma's innings was supported by Marco Jansen's 85 and Simon Harmer's 82, with the latter adding 183 runs with the captain. Praising their contributions, Bavuma said both batters played important roles in turning the innings around."Very brave innings from him," Bavuma said of Jansen, while he praised Harmer for showing "a lot of application" and felt the all-rounder was unlucky to miss out on a century.With South Africa having fought back into the contest, Bavuma said the batting unit had done its part and the responsibility now rested with the bowlers.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
Jansen (5-33) - who had already made a sizeable contribution after making 85 off 100 with the bat - led a ferocious Proteas bowling attack, aided by important contributions by the returning Kagiso Rabada (2-33) and all-rounder Wiaan Mulder (2-14), seeing off their opponents in just 42.4 overs.

articles.title: Jamie Overton would consider England Ashes return if asked by Joe Root
articles.summary: England all-rounder Jamie Overton would consider returning to play Test cricket for next year’s Ashes if approached by captain Joe Root.
articles.body:
England all-rounder Jamie Overton would consider returning to play Test cricket for next year's Ashes if approached by captain Joe Root.

Overton played in England's final Test of the home summer in 2025 against India and was in line for a place on last winter's Ashes tour, only to take what he described as an "indefinite break" from red-ball cricket.

The 32-year-old, who has a history of stress fractures in his back, has focused on limited-overs cricket since and is part of the England squad for the ongoing one-day tri-series in Pakistan.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Overton said England white-ball captain Harry Brook has asked about the possibility of the Surrey man making himself available for Test cricket.

"To be honest, I haven't thought about it," said Overton. "Brooky's mentioned it to me a couple of times, but I've literally not thought about it."

On the prospect of Root reaching out about the Ashes, Overton added: "If Rooty comes to me and says that then, yeah, then I'll have to have a serious think about it.

"I've always said it was an indefinite break. People think I've retired or whatever, but, no, it was a break that I could focus on my white-ball cricket and being really good in my white-ball cricket."

Overton's appearance in the fifth Test against India in July of 2025 was his second Test cap, three years after his first.

The pace bowler had played only four first-class matches in the two years leading up to his return to the Test team.

When England lost Chris Woakes to a dislocated shoulder, Overton was left as one of three frontline seamers in the XI and sent down 38 overs in the match.

A month later, he announced his hiatus from red-ball cricket, ruling himself out of the Ashes tour in the process.

Sloppy England start winter with Pakistan defeat

England coach should be English, suggests Fleming

"I came off that Test match against India and I felt physically broken," he said. "I know we lost the bowler, Wokesey went down with a shoulder injury, but that's the worst I felt in playing cricket for a long time.

"It nearly took me two weeks to get ready to play in The Hundred, when you only bowl 20 balls. My shoulder was incredibly sore for two weeks and it just felt like it was an injury waiting to happen if I kept trying to push myself.

"At that point I was just like: 'Let's focus on my white-ball and red-ball cricket might come back'. I've never said I've ruled it out completely."

In the aftermath of Ben Stokes' retirement, England have opted to field four frontline seamers in their XI, with Dan Lawrence batting at number six and offering some off-spin.

If England needed to alter the balance of their side, a returning Overton would be an option to strengthen their lower-order batting. He made 99 on his Test debut against New Zealand in 2022.

"I've never said I've ruled it out," said Overton. "It's just got to be the right thing at the right time.

"It's been just over a year and I've been really structured with my workloads and my plans and getting my body into a good spot. I feel really good."

Jamie's twin brother Craig has played in eight Tests, including in the Ashes series of 2017-18 and 2019.

Craig had a superb summer for Somerset, though told BBC Sport earlier this month he had not been contacted by England about the possibility of a recall.

For Jamie, after turning down the chance of a trip down under last year, Australia's visit to the UK next summer is likely to represent the last chance for a taste of Ashes cricket.

"At that moment I didn't feel like it was the right thing for my body," he said.

"The opportunity to play in the Ashes is every kid's dream. I watched Craig do it and was incredibly proud of what he did. Obviously, you want to be there and do it one day."

Overton was part of the England team beaten by Pakistan in their tri-series opener in Rawalpindi on Tuesday .

England meet Sri Lanka at the same ground on Thursday, with full commentary of that match on Test Match Special via BBC Sounds, BBC Radio 5 live sports extra and the BBC Sport website and app.
